source.title: Breaking the Architecture Barrier: A Method for Efficient Knowledge Transfer Across Networks
source.authors: Maciej A. Czyzewski; Danielle Nowak; Kamila Piechowiak

record.tranche_reason: The study trains randomly initialized networks and plots training accuracy, a different measure bearing on V1's training-error claim.
record.gate_note: Training-accuracy curves are shown in Figures 11 and 14. The text does not describe their values, so they are recorded as figure-only; test-accuracy results and cited prior-work claims are not rows.
record.test_reason: Figures 11's randomly initialized EfficientNet-B0 and B2 controls measure training classification accuracy on CIFAR-100 using Adam. Accuracy is the complement of classification error, so this uses V1's method and measure. The supplied text does not preserve curve values, preventing a directional verdict.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that DPIAT efficiently transfers pretrained parameters across CNN architectures and accelerates subsequent training compared with random and hypernetwork-based initialization. They acknowledge dependence on a suitable pretrained source and architectural similarity.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates inter-architecture parameter transfer and initialization, rather than testing the claim's stated training-error conditions as a primary question.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that transfer effectiveness varies with source-target architecture similarity and source training/domain; these are results about transfer and test accuracy, not V1 training error.

fits_no_version.finding: EfficientNet-B0 training accuracy on ImageNet is plotted for random and transferred initializations, but its values cannot be read from the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training classification accuracy of EfficientNet-B0 on ImageNet under different initializations.

fits_no_version.finding: DPIAT improves test accuracy and often reduces time to a test-accuracy threshold compared with random initialization; effectiveness depends on source-target similarity and source training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transferring pretrained parameters between CNN architectures can improve subsequent training efficiency and test accuracy.

record.problems: Training-accuracy outcomes relevant to V1 are shown only in figures, without descriptive text or extracted numeric values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional training-accuracy rows extracted beyond the two CIFAR100 targets and ImageNet target shown in Figures 11 and 14. Other reported results concern test accuracy, loss, transfer effectiveness, or cited work and do not establish the specified training-error finding.

untested.parts: Random or corrupted labels; training-error results on CIFAR-10; systematic effects of model size, early stopping, or regularization. The CIFAR-100 controls are relevant, but their outcomes cannot be read from the supplied text.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and controlled comparisons of plain networks with identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Activation-matched random initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth. Pretrained parameter transfer does not test these mechanisms.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, curvature dynamics, recovery, and divergence.
Controlled batch-normalization comparisons and training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: No directional verdict is justified by unreadable training-accuracy curves. Test accuracy and time to a test-accuracy threshold cannot establish near-zero training error. The already declared figure-only outcomes are not additional missing rows.

versions.untested_parts: Corrupted or random labels; CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 zero or near-zero error as a textual result; smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
